newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend fall, seen up on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend fall, seen up on Thursday.

text.p: Polish shares tumbled for the second day running and analysts said that after a rebound seen on Thursday, signalled by Wednesday's strong post-price-fixing, investors would remain focused on foreign bourses.

"The situation depends on the situation abroad and especially in New York--if things are calm there they'll be calm here and there will be a chance for growth," said Ryszard Wojnowski, an analyst Polish Investment Bank (PBI) brokerage.
Analysts said big falls in the U.S. could lead to the same in Warsaw, though some were unconvinced of a strong link with the Dow, saying that mostly local investors were selling.

"U.S. investors are not going to take money from emerging markets because the latter offer a very high return and a very high risk," said Mateusz Andrzejewski of Bank Pekao SA brokerage, referring to the recent U.S. Funds rate rise.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 3.1 percent to 15,596.2 points and turnover fell 22.7 percent to 173.1 million zlotys ($56.4 million) on all three markets. Loses led gainers by 69 to 13 with 11 stocks flat.

Analysts said several stocks had begun to look cheap after the market's fall from a three-year February 18 high at 18,339.4 points, with Andrzejewski putting support levels at 15,500 and 15,000 points.
Analysts were surprised by the scale of the 10-percent loss by carpet maker Novita in moderate trade.
They said bank BRE and industrial and trading firm Elektrim fell by nearly 10 percent in active trade after news earlier in the day that the companies had revised down 1996 earnings.
